thread:
alex: Quick question — when can we skip a semver bump for docs-only PRs? Releasebot suggested a patch for a README change and it's noisy.

pm_kate: Generally docs-only shouldn't force a public bump. We try to keep churn down. Releasebot heuristics look at changed paths and sometimes over-eagerly suggest a patch.

sam: Our rule: if there's no code/runtime/API change, mark PR `meta: docs-only` and add label `skip-release`. That prevents releasebot from incrementing.

deploy-bot: releasebot detected changed files: [docs/**, website/**], suggested bump: patch. To override add label `skip-release` or comment `/no-bump`.

jen: Can we standardize on a single override? Folks use `no-bump`, `skip-release`, `docs`. I'd prefer `skip-release` as canonical.

lia: Also watch out for borderline files: ci/config.yml or Dockerfile changes that are just docs vs actual runtime tweaks. If it touches Docker entrypoint or build args, treat as code.

sam: For customer-impacting hotfixes we follow the `hotfix` label flow: bump patch, pin to the dedicated channel, canary rollout (10%) with 30m observation. Rollback is a revert + redeploy of previous tag; we never reuse a semver once published.

alex: How do PMs/ops track skipped bumps so audit logs still show the change?

pm_kate: Add an entry to the internal changelog under "Docs (no-bump)" and push a one-line note to the release console UI. That makes it discoverable without inflating public versions.

jen: Suggested PR body snippet for the template:
```
meta: docs-only
release-notes: skip
labels: [skip-release]
```

sam: I'll update the runbook with the exact label and the comment override (`/no-bump`) so releasebot is deterministic. Also document the edgecases that force a bump.

lia: Thumbs up. Recommend adding a short reviewer checklist: "Does this touch runtime or public API?" Helps avoid accidental skips.

alex: Thanks — post the updated PR template snippet and I'll copy it into the repo now.

pm_kate: Pasting snippet above and will link the runbook when merged.
